title: Chapter 3:  International Political Economy (IPE)
content:
👋 ሰላም ተማሪዎቻችን! እንኳን ወደ EthioFresh የትምህርት መድረክ በደህና መጣችሁ! እኔ ከEthioFresh Team የ-International Relations እና Global Trends ትምህርት ባለሙያ ነኝ። በዚህ ክፍል የትምህርታችን ክፍል (Chapter 3 Part 2: Section 3.4 እስከ 3.5)፣ የዓለም አቀፍ ፖለቲካል ኢኮኖሚ ዋና ዋና ጉዳዮችን (International Trade, Investment, Finance)፣ አገዛዞችንና ተቋማትን (WTO, World Bank, IMF) እንዲሁም የምንዛሬ ሥርዓቶችን (Exchange Rate Systems) በጥልቀት እንመረምራለን። አብራችሁን ዝለቁ። መልካም ጥናት!

3.4. Core Issues, Governing Institutions and Governance of International Political Economy

International Political Economy (IPE) revolves around three core interrelated issues: International Trade, International Investment, and International Finance. Each issue area possesses its own specific governance structures, theoretical debates, and key international institutions designed to manage global economic interactions.

👉

🌐 የዓለም አቀፍ ፖለቲካል ኢኮኖሚ (IPE) በሶስት ዋና ዋና አምዶች ላይ የተመሰረተ ነው፦ እነሱም የዓለም አቀፍ ንግድ (Trade)፣ የዓለም አቀፍ ኢንቨስትመንት (Investment) እና የዓለም አቀፍ ፋይናንስ (Finance) ናቸው። እያንዳንዳቸው የራሳቸው ተቋማትና የፖለቲካ/ኢኮኖሚ ክርክሮች አሏቸው።

3.4.1. International Trade and the WTO

WTO (World Trade Organization): The World Trade Organization is an international organization that sets the rules for global trade. Established in 1995 as the successor to the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), which was created after the Second World War, the WTO has about 150 member countries. All decisions in the WTO are taken unanimously, but major economic powers such as the US, EU, and Japan have managed to use the WTO to frame trade rules that advance their own national interests. Developing countries often complain about non-transparent procedures and being pushed around by big powers.

Definition and Nature of Trade: Trade fundamentally involves the exchange of goods and services. For example, if someone gives you their laptop computer in exchange for your brand new iPad, you are engaged in trade—specifically referred to as barter trade. In the contemporary period, however, the vast majority of trade involves the exchange of money for goods and services, which can occur domestically or internationally.

Distinctions between Domestic and Cross-Border Trade: While cross-border trade involves the exchange of goods and services mediated by at least two different national governments—each exercising sovereign authority and pursuing its own interests—standard "free trade" defined as "the unrestricted purchase and sale of goods and services between countries without the imposition of constraints such as tariffs, duties, and quotas" is never entirely free in practice.

Scale of Trade and the Autarky Debate: Today, the scope and scale of cross-border trade is immensely greater than at any other point in human history. Liberal economists view this as natural because cross-border trade brings mutual benefit to individual national economies and the world as a whole. The general public acknowledges that the opposite of trade—autarky (a policy premised on complete economic independence or self-sufficiency)—is essentially impossible and self-defeating in industrial and post-industrial eras. Nevertheless, ongoing political and theoretical disputes persist over who benefits and who is harmed by trade.

Governance of Trade (FTAs, NAFTA, and Barriers): Global and regional free trade agreements govern international trade through institutions like the WTO or NAFTA (North American Free Trade Agreement between the US, Canada, and Mexico). Under NAFTA, tariffs were eliminated by mutual agreement in 2008, yet both Mexico and the US reserved rights to protect "import-sensitive sectors" via emergency safeguard measures if domestic producers face serious injury. Free trade agreements often retain protectionist or mercantilist tools, including tariffs (taxes on imported goods), import bans, and quantitative restrictions (import quotas). Furthermore, states utilize non-tariff barriers (NTBs), such as domestic health, safety, and environmental regulations, technical standards, and inspection requirements.

Theoretical Perspectives on Trade: Theoretical debates continue to mount alongside growing trade. Liberals emphasize the principle of comparative advantage. Mercantilists and Marxists counter by focusing on power differentials between national economies, class inequality, and economic exploitation.

👉

📦 ዓለም አቀፍ ንግድ እና WTO፡
• የንግድ ዓይነቶች፡ ንግድ ማለት የዕቃና አገልግሎት ልውውጥ ነው። ላፕቶፕ በአይፓድ መለወጥ የዕቃ በዕቃ ንግድ (Barter trade) ይባላል። በአሁኑ ጊዜ ግን አብዛኛው ንግድ በገንዘብ ይከናወናል。
• WTO (የዓለም ንግድ ድርጅት)፡ በ1995 እ.ኤ.አ. በGATT ምትክ የተቋቋመ ሲሆን የዓለም ንግድ ህጎችን ያወጣል። ውሳኔዎች በሙሉ ስምምነት (Unanimously) ቢያልፉም፣ እንደ አሜሪካ፣ አውሮፓ ህብረትና ጃፓን ያሉ ሀያላን ሀገራት ህጉን ለራሳቸው ጥቅም ያበጁታል፤ ታዳጊ ሀገራት ግን ይገለላሉ。
• Autarky (ራሱን የቻለ/የተዘጋ ኢኮኖሚ)፡ ራሱን ሙሉ በሙሉ የቻለና ከማንም ጋር የማይነግድ ኢኮኖሚ መገንባት በአሁኑ ጊዜ የማይቻልና ራስን መጎዳት ነው።
• የንግድ እንቅፋቶች (Trade Barriers)፦
1. Tariffs (ታሪፍ)፦ በገቢ ዕቃዎች ላይ የሚጣል ቀረጥ/ታክስ。
2. Quotas (ኮታ)፦ የሚገባውን ዕቃ መጠን መገደብ。
3. Non-Tariff Barriers (NTBs)፦ ታሪፍ ያልሆኑ ገደቦች (ለምሳሌ፦ የጤናና ደህንነት መስፈርቶች፣ የቴክኒክ ደረጃዎች)።

😅 EthioFresh Humor Break: በንግድ ቲዮሪ 'Autarky' ማለት ከማንም ሰው ጋር አለመገናኘት ማለት ነው! ልክ ፍሬሽማን እንደሆናችሁ Dorm ውስጥ ብቻችሁን ተቆልፎባችሁ ከጓደኞቻችሁ ዳቦ ለመበደር እንደመፍራት ማለት ነው! 😂
💡 Exam Hint: በፈተና ላይ "Which organization succeeded GATT in 1995?" ተብሎ ከተጠየቀ መልሱ WTO ነው! እንዲሁም Autarky ማለት "complete economic self-sufficiency" እንደሆነ አስታውሱ!

3.3.2. International Investment and the WB

World Bank (WB): Created immediately following the Second World War in 1945, the World Bank was primarily designed as a vehicle for the disbursement of Marshall Plan money to aid the immediate reconstruction of war-torn Europe. The end result succeeded in creating a financially, economically, and politically stable Europe. Later, the bank expanded its influence to developing countries in Asia, Africa, and Latin America. Its activities focus on human development (education, health), agriculture and rural development (irrigation, rural services), environmental protection, infrastructure (roads, urban regeneration, electricity), and governance (anti-corruption, legal institutions). It provides loans and grants to member countries, exercising enormous influence over their economic policies. Critics emphasize that the WB sets the economic agenda of poorer nations by attaching stringent conditions to its loans and forcing free market reforms ("one size fits all" neo-liberal prescriptions), often resulting in controversial or negative developmental impacts.

International/Transnational Production (Global FDI): Transnational production occurs when different parts of the overall production process for a single product take place across different national territories.

Case Study - Swedish Automobile Production: In the production of a single model of a Swedish automobile, at least 38 major and minor components are manufactured in factories spread throughout the world፦
• Hood latch cable: Manufactured by Klüster in Slovakia.
• Amplifier: Manufactured by Alpine in Japan.
• Engine control unit: Manufactured by Borgwarner in USA.
• Turbo diesel: Manufactured by Sanden in Japan.
• Drive shaft: Manufactured by GNK/Visteon in USA.
• Air conditioner: Manufactured by Valeo in France.
• Doors: Manufactured by Brose in Germany.

This case demonstrates that transnational production networks are vastly more complex, larger in scale, and wider in scope than at any other time in history. Key drivers include drastic decreases in transport and communications costs, making global production economically efficient, the rise of efficiency-seeking Foreign Direct Investments (FDIs) worldwide, technological advancements, and improved global financial integration.

👉

🏦 የዓለም ባንክ (World Bank) እና ዓለም አቀፍ ኢንቨስትመንት፡
• የዓለም ባንክ አመሰራረት፡ በ1945 ተመሰረተ። የመጀመሪያ ዓላማው ከ2ኛው የዓለም ጦርነት በኋላ አውሮፓን በMarshall Plan ገንዘብ ለመልሶ ግንባታ መረዳት ነበር። በኋላ ግን ትኩረቱን ወደ ታዳጊ ሀገራት (እስያ፣ አፍሪካ፣ ላቲን አሜሪካ) አዞረ።
• ትችት፡ የዓለም ባንክ ለድሃ ሀገራት ብድር ሲሰጥ ጥብቅ የነፃ ገበያ መስፈርቶችን (Conditions) በማስቀመጡና "One size fits all" ፖሊሲ በመከተሉ ከፍተኛ ትችት ይቀርብበታል።
• የስዊድን መኪና ምሳሌ (Global Supply Chain)፡ አንድ የስዊድን መኪና ለማምረት የ38 ሀገራት አካላት ይሳተፋሉ። ለምሳሌ ሞተሩ ከአሜሪካ፣ ኤርኮንዲሽነሩ ከፈረንሳይ፣ በሩ ከጀርመን ወዘተ። ይህም የዓለም አቀፍ ምርት (FDI) ምን ያህል እንደተሳሰረ ያሳያል።

3.4.3. International Finance and the IMF

International Monetary Fund (IMF): The International Monetary Fund is an international organization that oversees financial institutions and regulations acting at the international level. The IMF has 184 member countries, but voting power is not equal. The top ten countries hold 55 percent of the total votes. These are the G-8 members (US, Japan, Germany, France, UK, Italy, Canada, Russia), Saudi Arabia, and China. The US alone possesses 17.4 percent of the voting rights, giving it effective veto power. The IMF was designed to represent US interests and power first and foremost, and secondarily the interests of major developed capitalist economies. Decision-making power is determined by a "quota" (capital subscription)—the amount of money a member country pays to the IMF. The more a country pays, the more say it has.

Structure of the Global Financial System: The global financial system consists of two separate but tightly interrelated systems፦
1. Monetary System: Defined as the relationship between and among national currencies, revolving around how exchange rates are determined.
2. Credit System: Refers to the framework of rules, agreements, institutions, and practices that facilitate the transnational flow of financial capital for investment and trade financing.

👉

💵 IMF እና የዓለም አቀፍ ፋይናንስ ሥርዓት፡
• IMF (ዓለም አቀፍ የገንዘብ ድርጅት)፦ 184 አባል ሀገራት አሉት። ነገር ግን ውሳኔ የሚሰጠው በክፍያ መጠን (Quota) ነው። አሜሪካ ብቻዋን 17.4% የድምፅ ድርሻ ስላላት ትልቅ ተፅዕኖ አላት። ዋና ዋናዎቹ 10 ሀገራት 55% ድምፅ ይቆጣጠራሉ።
• የፋይናንስ ሥርዓት ክፍሎች፦
1. Monetary System (የገንዘብ ሥርዓት)፦ በሀገራት ገንዘቦች መካከል ያለውን የምንዛሬ ተመን ይቆጣጠራል።
2. Credit System (የብድር/ካፒታል ሥርዓት)፦ ለኢንቨስትመንትና ንግድ የካፒታል ዝውውርን ያመቻቻል።

💡 Exam Hint: IMF ውስጥ ድምፅ የሚሰጠው "One country, one vote" በሚል ሳይሆን በQuota (የገንዘብ አስተዋፅኦ) መጠን እንደሆነ በደማቅ ያዙ! አሜሪካ 17.4% ድምፅ አላት።

3.5. Exchange Rates and the Exchange-Rate System

An exchange rate is the price of one national currency in terms of another.

Historical Numerical Examples of Currency Value Fluctuations:
• July 2013 Rate: 1 US Dollar ($1) = 98.1 Japanese Yen (¥); 1 British Pound (£) = 1.54 US Dollars ($1.54).
• August 1998 Rate: 1 US Dollar ($1) = 145.8 Japanese Yen (¥).
• Comparison: Between August 1998 and July 2013, the difference in the value of the Yen against the Dollar was nearly 50 percent. In August 1998, the Yen was substantially "weaker".
• Concrete Example ($2,000 Travel Budget): In 1998, traveling to Japan with $2,000 allowed you to exchange it for 291,000 Yen. In 2013, that same $2,000 yielded only 196,000 Yen. Thus, you had significantly less Yen to spend in 2013 due to currency fluctuations.

Two Main Exchange Rate Systems:
1. Floating Exchange Rate System: In a pure floating-rate system, the value of a currency is determined solely by market forces—money supply and money demand—without any government or nonmarket intervention.
2. Fixed Exchange Rate System: In a pure fixed-rate system, the value of a particular currency is pegged/fixed against the value of another single currency (e.g., US Dollar) or against a basket of currencies.

👉

🎚️ የምንዛሬ ተመን (Exchange Rates)፦ የአንድ ሀገር ገንዘብ በሌላ ሀገር ገንዘብ ሲመነዘር ያለው ዋጋ ነው።
• ለምሳሌ ፦ በ1998 እ.ኤ.አ. 2,000 ዶላር ወደ ጃፓን ይዘው ቢሄዱ 291,000 የን ያገኙ ነበር፤ በ2013 ግን ያው 2,000 ዶላር ያመጣው 196,000 የን ብቻ ነው። ምክንያቱም የን በ2013 ከ1998 አንፃር ስለጠነከረ ነው።
• ሁለቱ የምንዛሬ ሥርዓቶች፦
1. Floating (ተለዋዋጭ የምንዛሬ ተመን)፦ ዋጋው በገበያ ፍላጎትና አቅርቦት (Supply & Demand) ብቻ ይወሰናል፤ የመንግሥት ጣልቃ ገብነት የለም。
2. Fixed (የተወሰነ/የተቸከለ የምንዛሬ ተመን)፦ ዋጋው ከአንድ ጠንካራ ገንዘብ (ለምሳሌ ከዶላር) ጋር እንዲዛመድ ተደርጎ በመንግሥት ይወሰናል。

✨ የዛሬው የChapter 3 ሙሉ የቱቶሪያል ኖታችን በዚሁ ተጠናቅቋል። ቀጣይ በ CHAPTER 4 እስክንገናኝ ደህና ሁኑ።
